column1: # Step 2 (02-rdd-to-dataset): what each scored family is worth.
# Since 2026-10-13 (user decision, product scoring) the two families are
# multiplied, not added: reward = T1 x T2, where T1 is the migrated family's
# points over its total weight below and T2 is the behavior family's points
# over its total weight below (score.py, product_reward). The weights still
# sum to 1; they now set the proportions inside each factor. Where the prose
# below speaks of a family's share of the reward, read it as that family's
# share before this change.
# Two families, as rule 5 requires, and neither below ~30%:
#   behavior   0.30   the tree still does what it did      replay + the repo's own tests
#   migrated   0.70   fifteen named classes take their terminal result through
#                     the SQL engine, and nothing was handed to that engine as
#                     an opaque blob to get it there
# The rung does not move at this step. Step 1 landed on Spark 3.0.3 / Scala
# 2.12 and step 2 stays there: this is a code move, not a version move, and
# `environment/` is byte-identical to step 1's. That changes what the behavior
# family can be graded on, and the change is the only interesting thing in this
# file.
# The same sentence has to be true here -- section 8 of migration_prompt.md:
# the nop reports 0.0 -- and it is a live risk rather than a formality. The nop
# tree at step 2 is still the untouched 2.4 tree (a nop run does nothing at
# step 1 either), that tree still builds against the /opt/spark 3.0.3 in the
# image, and it reproduces most of these 140 recordings. Left ungated, this
# step's nop would score about 0.28 for changing nothing.
# Step 1 held that line with `spark_line_moved`, which asks the resolved
# dependency graph whether the build still says Spark 2.4. Reused here it would
# zero the nop too, so the reason not to reuse it is not that it fails. The
# reason is that at step 2 it is `held-m1-spark-303` restated: a claim about
# step 1's work, which Harbor hands this step's candidate already done. It
# would grade this step's behavior on a precondition instead of on this step's
# move, and it would pay in the wrong direction -- step 1's finished solution
# does none of step 2's work, resolves 3.0.3, and would collect all 0.30 of it.
# So the gate is this step's own question, read from this step's own facts:
# `dataset_terminal_reached` in score.py is true when one of the sixteen scoped
# rows cleared the threshold its own m02.tsv rule sets for it *and* one of the
# fifteen scoped classes shows the whole move in the built jar -- no `count` or
# `reduce` on a JavaRDD, an RDD handed to `createDataset`/`createDataFrame`, a
# result read back off the `Dataset`. The rows are read out of the same
# gateroot/probe.tsv the m1..m4 rules are read from, the three artifact rules
# out of the same gate report those requirements are scored from, and the
# patterns and thresholds are parsed out of m02.tsv rather than kept as a
# second list in score.py, so `scoped` cannot come to mean two things.
# The conjunction is round 1's fix and is the whole of it. The probe rows are
# written by a listener inside the candidate's own driver JVM, so the run half
# alone is forgeable from a shutdown hook; `-rdd-gone` alone is bought by
# deleting the count and printing the constant it used to print, because the
# corpus is fixed and stdout still matches. Neither half is the claim; together
# they are. What the pair still cannot see is dataflow -- a Dataset built from
# `sc.parallelize(ONE)` satisfies the artifact half from the constant pool --
# and NOTES 6.2.7 records that residual rather than hiding it.
# It is otherwise the weakest condition that separates a tree which made the
# move from one that did not: one row and one class, each judged the way its
# own rules judge it, and a candidate who migrated one of the fifteen classes
# and gave up keeps every point of proportional behavior credit and loses only
# the requirements that measure the other fourteen. There is no cliff here for
# anybody who tried.
# The thresholds are not decoration. Written first as "one scoped job inside
# one execution", this gate was green on the untouched tree: AuthorSearchDemo,
# KeywordSearch and KinaseSearch each run two real SQL executions before the
# step begins, because PdbjMineSearch's constructor reads its query through the
# engine. Their rules ask for three for that reason, and the gate honours the
# same three. NOTES 6.2.6 records the measurement that caught it.
# What that costs, stated rather than hidden: the item-6 floor -- step 1's
# finished solution scored by this verifier -- reports 0.0 rather than the 0.30
# it would report if behavior were graded unconditionally. Both satisfy item 6's
# "<=0.5"; 0.0 was chosen because step 2 is not paid for step 1's work at all
# (that is what `hold m01.tsv` means) and a behavior family that paid 0.30 for
# an inherited tree would be paying for it. The rejected alternative -- gating
# behavior on the migrated family not being void, which would have given the
# floor 0.30 and the nop 0.0 as well -- is recorded with its reasoning in
# NOTES 6.2.6.
# Within `migrated`, a requirement scores all or nothing: every rule carrying
# its prefix must be PASS. Fourteen of fifteen classes migrated is not fourteen
# fifteenths of an API move; the reason to split the fifteen into four
# requirements rather than one is that each group is a *different edit*, so
# each all-or-nothing verdict is over work a candidate either understood or did
# not:
#   m1  read MMTF, maybe filter, count            7 classes / 8 scored rows
#   m2  count what a flatMapToPair produced       4 classes
#   m3  reduce a mapped value to a total          1 class
#   m4  count behind a web-service filter         3 classes
# m1 is the largest because it is seven classes and the move's canonical shape:
# build a typed Dataset off the reader's RDD and take the count there. m2 is
# the same move one stage down a pipeline and is worth less per class because a
# candidate who did m1 has learned everything m2 needs except where to put it.
# m3 is one class and is worth 0.12 because it is the only row where the answer
# is not a count -- `map(t -> numAtoms).reduce(+)` becomes an aggregate over a
# typed column, and the printed total has to come back the same Java long. m4
# is three classes and is worth more than m3 because those three already have
# SQL executions in them before the step begins: getting them right means
# reading what the probe actually reports rather than copying the shape of the
# other twelve rules, and getting them wrong is the easiest way to lose points
# here while believing the work is done.
# Thirteen rules carry no `m<digit>-` prefix and so are standing rules rather
# than requirements. Nine are in gates/rules/cheats.tsv -- the opaque encoder
# and the setLocalProperty call, each read off the sources, out of the jar's
# references and out of its constant pool, plus the forged-execution-id rule,
# plus the two that catch a jar reaching for the listener this gate reads its
# job rows from -- and score.py reads those nine out of that file by name,
# which is what makes
# their price the *whole* reward rather than the migrated family's share. The
# other four are in m02.tsv: the two that keep MmtfReader's RDD contract, the
# one that says the replay ran with the listener attached at all, and the one
# that says no submit this verifier made exited non-zero. A tree that bought
# the job rules with `Encoders.kryo` or with one `setLocalProperty` call does
# not lose a share, it loses the reading -- which is what a tree that faked the
# step is worth, and which the instruction says in as many words. The reasoning
# is in those files beside the rules.
# Each requirement is now three artifact rules per class plus its runtime
# row(s): sixty-four scored rules over the four families, up from thirty-four
# before round 1. The split between the families is unchanged -- what changed
# is how much each class has to show, not what each family is worth.
# Within `behavior`, credit is proportional and the unit is rule 7's scored
# input -- the same 247 at this census as at step 1, because this step is
# required to change none of them. The recordings are `build/p02/`: the step-1
# golden tree's own 140 outputs at this rung, replayed with gate.GateProbe
# attached, which is the configuration this step's verifier runs (NOTES 6.2.4
# proved the listener changes none of the 140).
# 40m35s end to end, on 7 vCPU, from this step's first phase header to its
# reward.json: the oracle run of 2026-09-18 (jobs dir m27-s3-oracle, job
# 27-spark24-to-4.0__k7shaVo), taken while another agent's jobs shared the
# box, so it is an upper reading rather than a clean one. Rule 10 aims at
# ~30 minutes a step and caps at 60. The 140-job replay is the bulk of it:
# the inherited suite does not open until 36m12s;
# neither the replay's 140 jobs nor the suite's 142 tests is reducible
# without asking a smaller question, and rule 10's own instruction is not
# to shrink a fixture set to fit a clock.
# family
